physDesc.additional: Script: dpe tshugs. Folio numbered with letters (only ga, cha and ja are visible). Lines per folio; 11; 10 on fol. 6b; 8 on fol. 7a. Orthography: - Abbreviations (e.g., for slob dpon, thams cad, final –gs, etc.) - Bindu for m - Numerals used for numbers and for phonetic value (e.g., 4+n for bzhin) - Frequent broken shad ( ¦ ), sometimes used in place of tsheg. - Alternative prefixes (e.g., rngos for dngos) - la rtsogs pa for la sogs pa - ṇa (reversed form of na) for med - Tibetan numerals used for numbers (e.g. 2 po for gnyis po) - gzhan written with "n" below the leg of "zh". Several annotations (corrections as well as glosses). A da-drag is used in an annotation on fol. 4b8 ('phrind).

gang gis rdzogsrtzog‹s› pa'i byang chub du ||
thugs bskyed bslab pa'i mthar phyin ste ||
brtse bas nyid zhugs lam ston pa ||
skyob pa mchog la phyag 'tshal lo || || I bow down to the supreme protector, who generated the exalted mind toward the complete enlightenment and accomplished the discipline and indicates the path that [he] entered [to it] by means of mercy itself.
zab cing rgya che rigs dang ldan pas kyang ||
{kya} snyed dka'rka yon tan kun gyi gter gyur pa ||
rgyal sras sdom pa'i tshig le'ur bcas pa ni ||‹||›
don rdzog lung
rigs ldan par rnam bshad bya ||The verses on the vow of the Conqueror’s sons are a treasure of all merits, which is difficult to be obtained even by those endowed with a profound and extensive reasoning. These verses are to be explained in their entire meaning, together with reason and scriptures. (Alternatively: Concerning these verses, an explanation of their full meaning will be done, endowed with reason as well as scriptures. {This second option takes "rnam bshad" as a noun; this is supported by author’s description of his work as a “rnam bshad” in the closing section})

seg.note: [Although] no one previously has explained this text {this might refer to the absence of a previous commentary of this base text (gzhung 'di), or to the fact that nobody explained the base text in the way he does in this text (gzhung 'dir)}, using the Boddhisattva’s Collections and instructions, I have made an explanation that clarifies the meaning of the words of what constitutes the training in moral conduct of the Conqueror’s sons [the Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśaka].

lg.l: dge ba 'di yis tsha rabs kun tu bdag ||
byang chub sems dang mthu yis dpa' rnams kyi ||
zab yangs ngo mtshar rmad kyi spyod pa la ||
mi 'jigs brtson 'grus seng ge'i stobs ldan shog || ||

seg.note: Thanks to the virtue [of composing] this [commentary], in all [my future] lives, may I have fearlessness, diligence, and the lion’s strength {Alternatively: may I have the strength of a fearless diligent lion}, towards profound, extensive, wonderful, and marvelous practice of heroes, by means of the mind and the power of Bodhi.
